keyFindings.description: Fast-follow, not a gate: the session-proxy helpers and scenarios (echoUpstream, holdSessionSocket, expectHeldClosed and the external-holder tests) took the general launcher test file from 853 to 1,137 lines; they belong in a session-proxy test file of their own beside session_store_test.go.

roundOneResolved: PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v_exS (proof dial without a deadline): fixed in 00b13caf9d26, bounded at half --stop-grace, inside the daemon's start wait (awaitRoleLauncher deadline plus terminationGrace, relaunch.go:174-178,301-341).

PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v_exT (Close waits on copies it never closes): fixed in 523b2d19173f, drains for sessionDrain (1 s) then closes every tracked pair; pairs dialed after closing are closed in track; close_race_test.go pins it.
PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v_exX (docs lifetime bound): fixed in 2d69ffa95092, both the stop and natural-exit cases stated.
PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6v_exZ (ValidInstance): fixed in b80c9de6821a, ParseConnName plus a whole-string round trip plus no whitespace.
residualRisk: The 30 s resume lookup after a successful proof can outlast the daemon's start wait for a launcher that connects in the last seconds of a new pod's boot window. That budget is the same one postgres already has on main, it needs the database to fail between a successful proof and the lookup, it frees the command loop within 30 s, and the daemon's retry into the now-bound pod has the full boot-timeout budget, so the named refusal reaches it then. Both thermonuclear agents rated it Medium/Important; recorded as risk, not a finding.
